# Your report


We initialized the text-mining pipeline by using load_dataset_tool (result_id: load_dataset_1), yielding 847 Reddit posts across three sentiment classes: 423 neutral (0.0), 315 negative (-1.0), and 109 positive (1.0). Data hygiene was evaluated through check_missing_tool (result_id: check_missing_2), confirming 0 missing values across all columns, while check_duplicates_tool (result_id: check_duplicates_3) identified 23 duplicate posts. Subsequent character length profiling using describe_data_tool (result_id: describe_data_4) revealed severe positive skewness characteristic of short-form social media commentary: documents exhibited an overall mean length of 148.68 characters and a median of 79 characters, bounded by a 1-character minimum and a 2,753-character maximum. Positive posts showed the highest mean length (164.64 characters), whereas negative posts had a higher median (96 characters), contrasting sharply with the long-form documents of the 20 Newsgroups corpus.
![Document Length Distributions Across Categories](../plots/Hajer_Mastouri_homework_plot_describe_data_4.png)

Following initial inspection, raw texts were tokenized using tokenize_tool (result_id: tokenize_5), extracting 26,386 unigram tokens at an average of 31.15 tokens per post. We transformed this vocabulary into vector space using build_dtm_tool (result_id: dtm_6) with frequency cutoffs (min_df=2, max_df=0.8). This constructed an 847 × 1,711 Document-term Matrix comprising 14,558 non-zero entries and an extreme sparsity rate of 98.996%. To inspect the underlying structure, dtm_heatmap_tool (result_id: dtm_heatmap_7) rendered a 20 × 20 positional submatrix. Due to alphabetical indexing, leading columns were dominated by numeric and temporal tokens ('00', '000', '10', '100', '125'), which registered zero occurrences across almost all initial documents, with isolated counts appearing only in Document 9 and Document 13. 
![Document-Term Matrix Heatmap](../plots/Hajer_Mastouri_homework_plot_dtm_heatmap_7.png)

To isolate informative terms, we first applied variance_filter_tool (result_id: variance_filter_8), which removed most low-variance words but left high-frequency stopwords alongside core market terms (market/money..). Using this filtered vocabulary, mine_patterns_tool (result_id: patterns_9) extracted top frequent keywords for negative posts (-1.0). Unlike in the 20 Newsgroups, these patterns captured meaningful economics and geopolitical themes such as trump, china, market. 
Because variance filtering retained generic stopwords, we tested a supervised approach using spearman_filter_tool (result_id: spearman_filter_11) against negative sentiment (-1.0). This rank-correlation filter pruned the vast majority of vocabulary and isolated words directly tied to negative polarity such as trade tensions, political mentions, and emotional words. This proved far more effective for sentiment discrimination than unsupervised variance filtering.

Finally, we projected the variance-filtered matrix into 2D space using reduce_dimensions_tool (result_id: reduction_10, PCA). Rather than separating into distinct topical rays like 20 Newsgroups, the Reddit posts overlap in a dense cluster near the origin, with only a few posts stretching out as extreme outliers. Because PCA ran on raw word counts, the first principal component mainly reflected post length rather than sentiment. This confirmed that short texts and high sparsity require length normalization and supervised feature selection for effective text mining.
![2D Dimension Reduction (PCA)](../plots/Hajer_Mastouri_homework_plot_reduction_10.png)
